macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks rise as investors weigh possible Fed leadership change
items.summary: The Dow gained about 200 points, while the S&P 500 approached a record and the Nasdaq advanced. Markets reacted to signals that President Trump may seek a replacement for Fed Chair Jerome Powell, raising expectations of future rate cuts, while Nvidia led major stock movers.

items.title: Soft producer-price data offers limited relief on Fed rate concerns
items.summary: U.S. producer prices rose 0.3% in October, slightly below expectations, but traders still priced in a December rate increase and considered the possibility of a larger 50-basis-point move. Treasury yields and the dollar remained sensitive to shifting policy expectations.

items.title: Nvidia weakness weighs on technology stocks
items.summary: A selloff in chipmakers pressured equities, with the semiconductor gauge falling sharply and Nvidia facing concerns after Jensen Huang’s resignation and Colette Kress’s appointment as interim CEO. The S&P 500 fell 0.4% and the Nasdaq 100 declined 1.2% in the latest session covered.

items.title: Cerebras raises forecast and signs Microsoft as customer
items.summary: AI-chip and cloud company Cerebras raised its 2026 revenue forecast and announced Microsoft as a customer, sending its shares sharply higher in premarket trading. The development adds to competition around Nvidia in the artificial-intelligence chip market.

items.title: FedEx cuts earnings outlook as shares fall
items.summary: FedEx reduced its earnings outlook, sending the stock down 6.5% and raising concerns about the strength of freight demand and the broader economy. The company’s results were highlighted as a key economic bellwether.

items.title: AstraZeneca announces $2.5 billion China investment
items.summary: AstraZeneca said it will invest $2.5 billion in a Beijing research-and-development center through a partnership with Chinese authorities. The project expands the company’s long-term presence in China.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin falls below $70,000 as crypto liquidations surge
items.summary: Bitcoin dropped to a daily low near $67,500 before recovering to around $69,552, while approximately $1.65 billion in crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours. Bitcoin accounted for about $918.6 million of those liquidations.[2]

items.title: Strategy adds 1,036 Bitcoin to treasury
items.summary: Strategy reportedly purchased an additional 1,036 BTC, bringing its total holdings to 850,364 BTC. The company also repurchased $188 million of STRC shares.[1]

items.title: Coinbase receives approval for national trust company
items.summary: Coinbase received final approval from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to launch Coinbase National Trust Company, expanding its federally regulated custody operations.[1][7]

items.title: NYSE selects Avalanche for tokenized securities settlement
items.summary: The New York Stock Exchange selected Avalanche to provide the core clearing and settlement infrastructure for a planned 24/7 tokenized-securities platform, subject to regulatory approval.[1]

items.title: Project Faro stablecoin venture secures $270 million commitment
items.summary: Goldman Sachs, Citi and other banks reportedly committed $270 million to fund five years of operations for Project Faro, a joint stablecoin initiative involving 21 financial institutions. The dollar-based stablecoin is planned for launch in the first half of 2027.[1]

items.title: Bitcoin Core patches three security vulnerabilities
items.summary: Bitcoin Core disclosed three patched security flaws, including a high-severity vulnerability related to mining.[1]

items.title: Gnosis Pay reports data breach
items.summary: Gnosis Pay suffered a data breach that exposed sensitive information including names, home addresses, banking details and linked crypto addresses. No loss of funds was reported.[1]

items.title: Solana spot ETF records net outflows
items.summary: Solana spot ETFs saw approximately $3.09 million in net outflows on November 13, with Fidelity’s FSOL accounting for the entire daily decline.[4]

items.title: Solana launches confidential-computing tool for private AI
items.summary: The Solana Foundation launched Confidential Compute on Devnet in collaboration with Nito AI, enabling private AI applications with on-chain hardware-attestation verification.[4]

items.title: Galxe winds down several Web3 services
items.summary: Web3 rewards platform Galxe is shutting down Galxe Quest, Galxe ID, Galxe Passport and related services, with the company focusing future efforts on its Gravity layer-1 network.[1]
